name: python
description:
Run Python code in a persistent session (variables persist across calls, like a notebook). numpy is available as `np` and torch as `torch` (CPU only, 2 threads). `weights` is a dict of read-only, memory-mapped float32 numpy arrays (use np.array(a) for a writable copy), torch nn.Linear layout [out, in]. Model X tensors (Model Y has the same names with the prefix `Y.`):
  X.layers.0.input_layernorm.weight: [640]
  X.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.weight: [640, 2048]
  X.layers.0.mlp.gate_proj.weight: [2048, 640]
  X.layers.0.mlp.up_proj.weight: [2048, 640]
  X.layers.0.post_attention_layernorm.weight: [640]
  X.layers.0.post_feedforward_layernorm.weight: [640]
  X.layers.0.pre_feedforward_layernorm.weight: [640]
  X.layers.0.self_attn.k_norm.weight: [256]
  X.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.weight: [256, 640]
  X.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.weight: [640, 1024]
  X.layers.0.self_attn.q_norm.weight: [256]
  X.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.weight: [1024, 640]
  X.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj.weight: [256, 640]
  (same for layers 1-17)
Shared (frozen, identical in both): shared.embed_tokens.weight [262144, 640], shared.norm.weight [640]. `vocab` = list of 262144 token strings.
Functions:
attention(model, texts, positions="last", spans=None, chat=True, assistant_prefix=None) -> dict   [budget: 15 calls; failed calls are not counted; budget_status() is free]
  Runs Model X and/or Y on your texts and returns ONLY attention patterns (no outputs, logits or hidden states).
  model: "X", "Y" or "both" (same texts through both models in one call; returns {"X": res, "Y": res}).
  texts: list of up to 8 strings; each must be <= 256 tokens after formatting.
  chat=True: each text becomes one user turn in the Gemma chat format, followed by the model-turn header "<start_of_turn>model\n"; assistant_prefix (optional string) is appended after the header, i.e. a start of the model's reply that you write. The last position is then where the model would predict its next token. chat=False: raw text with <bos> prepended.
  positions: query positions to report: "last", an int, or a list of up to 8 ints (negative ok).
  spans: optional dict name -> span (up to 8); a span is a substring (its LAST occurrence in the formatted text; prefix "first:" for the first), [char_start, char_end] in the formatted text, or {"tokens": [token indices]}. Returns the summed attention from each query position to the span.
  res = {"tokens": [token strings per text], "formatted": [formatted text per text], "query_positions": [list per text], "from_positions": [array [18, 4, n_query, T] per text], "span_attention": [{name: array [18, 4, n_query]} per text], "span_token_idx": [{name: [indices]} per text], "layer_types": [...]}. Values are post-softmax attention probabilities (each row sums to 1 over keys); axes are [layer, head, query position, key position].
stdout and the value of the last expression are returned (truncated to 20000 chars). Each call times out after 180s. No file system or network access.
